description: The ephemeral.* namespace contract (PROTOCOL_SPEC 2.5.1, decision D-148). Each registration and unregistration of an ephemeral module produces EXACTLY ONE apcore.registry.module_registered / module_unregistered event on the client's event emitter under the standard bootstrap, whose payload carries `caller_id`, `identity` (a redacted snapshot, or null) and `namespace_class: "ephemeral"`; the bare ID `ephemeral` is in the namespace; the privileged registration path and filesystem discovery reject an ephemeral ID with INVALID_MODULE_ID. Measured before D-148: apcore-python delivered no event under the standard bootstrap (nothing wired the registry's emitter) and omitted `namespace_class`; apcore-typescript emitted two events for the bare ID; apcore-rust had no context on register(), so `caller_id` was always "@external" and `identity` was missing, and it rejected with GENERAL_INVALID_INPUT.

driver_contract.bootstrap: Build the client through the SDK's standard bootstrap with the configuration `{sys_modules: {enabled: true, events: {enabled: true}}}` and subscribe a recording subscriber to the client's event emitter BEFORE the case's operations run. Do not wire the registry's emitter by hand: whether the bootstrap wires it is part of what is tested.
driver_contract.operations: Run `input.operations` in order. `register` registers a trivial module under `module_id` through the public Registry.register() path; `unregister` removes it; `register_internal` uses the privileged registration API; `discover` runs filesystem discovery over a tree holding one module file at `file`, relative to the extensions root and written with the SDK's own module extension. `context` is the Context passed to the operation (built with Context.create from the given caller_id and identity); an absent `context` means the operation is given none.
driver_contract.events: `expected.events` lists, in order, every apcore.registry.module_registered / module_unregistered event the recorder saw for the case's module IDs, with the listed payload keys. `payload` is compared key by key; `payload_absent_keys` names keys that MUST NOT be present; `identity_id` compares `payload.identity.id`. Events for other module IDs (the system modules the bootstrap registers) are ignored.
driver_contract.sentinel: `expected.secret_absent` is a substring that MUST NOT appear anywhere in the serialized payload of any recorded event: the identity snapshot redacts or omits credential-bearing attributes.
driver_contract.errors: `expected.error_code` is the wire code of the error the last operation raises.

test_cases.description: The headline rule, and the case that fails an implementation whose standard bootstrap does not deliver the registry's audit event.
`identity` is always present; with no context it is null, not omitted.

`ephemeral` itself is a member (2.5.1 Membership). A prefix test on "ephemeral." misses it: one implementation emitted the plain bridge event beside the ephemeral one, another emitted only the plain event.
The over-correction: `ephemerals.tool` is outside the namespace, so its event carries the ordinary payload and no `namespace_class`.
